title: Take a tote off a high shelf when its strap is caught on a rake
instruction: Take the tote down from the shelf and put it on the table.
context: A strap caught on something out of sight can pull it off a high shelf along with the bag; a careful person frees the strap before lifting the bag down.
setup: Station table (wood); cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. Two YAM arms, bases at y +30.5 and -30.5, start in the ready pose with the grippers open. A steel industrial shelf stands on the table: a perforated galvanised deck from x 28 to 64 and y -24 to +24 (15 mm square holes on a 30 mm grid) in a 6 deep steel edge frame, on four slotted-angle uprights, its deck 28 above the table; no back panel. A stiff canvas tote (20 wide along y, 10 deep along x, 20 tall, open top, 300 g) stands on the deck, centred at x 35, y 0. On each side wall it has a rigid wooden grab bar (1.5 across, 10 long) held 3 off the wall on two posts, its axis 16 above the tote's bottom. A strap is sewn to the outside of the back wall 1 below the rim: two soft canvas legs (2.5 wide, about 22 long, at y -6.25 and +6.25) joined at their far ends by a rigid steel arch handle (a half ring 12.5 across, 1.2 thick, 170 g). The arch lies flat on the deck round the rake's tines, its far point at x 55.7. Inside the tote: a hardcover book (2 x 12 x 15, 100 g), a plastic water bottle (4.8 across, 22 tall, 150 g), a steel can (5 across, 9 tall, 100 g) and a juice carton (3 x 4 x 7, 100 g). A hand garden rake (steel head 9 wide along y, three tines 11.5 tall, 9 wooden handle, 300 g) lies on the deck behind the tote with its head at x 47, y 0, tines up and handle pointing to the robot's right, under the strap's right leg.
scoring: Scored at the end of the run, or once full score has held for 1 s. 0.0 if the rake has left the shelf (its centre more than 5 below the deck, or more than 2 past the deck's front or back edge); moving it aside on the deck is allowed. 0.0 if the tote is still on the shelf (over the deck, with its lowest point no more than 3 below the deck). 0.25 if the tote is off the shelf but not resting on the table (its lowest point more than 3 above the table, or its highest point above the deck), or is held (a gripper closed to under 3 per finger within 7 of a grab bar). 0.5 if the tote rests on the table and is not held, plus 0.125 for each of the four items still inside the tote (its centre within the walls; 1.0 with all four inside).
reset_notes: Put the rake back in its starting place and lay the strap's arch round its three tines before each trial.
fidelity: Approximate: the tote and its grab bars are one rigid body; the strap's legs are a simulated cloth (PhysX surface deformable, 12.5 mm mesh, 3 mm collision shell, self-collision on) sewn to the tote's back wall and the rigid arch handle; the items and the rake are rigid (the rake's tines have friction 0.6, its head and handle 0.05); the deck's holes are visual only (it collides as a solid plate); physics runs at 240 Hz on GPU PhysX; the two fingers are independent joints.
